The finding is thus about the packet's own construction, not about a misreading of SRC-0004. LIVE PRIMARY VERIFICATION OF THE MATHEMATICAL POINT. (1) Pagani-Ricolfi-van Zelm, 'Pullbacks of universal Brill-Noether classes via Abel-Jacobi morphisms' (arXiv:1809.10668), Section 3.2: the universal Brill-Noether locus is given set-theoretically as {(C,P,L) : L in Pic^d C, h^0(C,L) > r} and then 'can be endowed with the scheme structure of the (g-d+r)-th Fitting ideal of R^1 pi_* L'. The scheme structure is IMPOSED by a separate definition, not read off from the set-theoretic description; and the paper's entire subject is the comparison of such universal classes with their pullbacks along Abel-Jacobi morphisms, treated as a substantive computation (Thom-Porteous class w^r_d = Delta^{(r+1)}_{g-d+r} c(-R pi_* L)). This is direct primary support for the finding's core assertion. (2) arXiv:2405.17689 constructs Brill-Noether ideals BN^k(F) = I_{r_0-k}(delta^0), the ideal of (r_0-k)x(r_0-k) minors of delta^0 for a base-change complex (a bounded complex of locally free sheaves with R^i (f_T)_* F_T iso h^i(E_T^.) for any T -> Y), i.e. exactly the determinantal/Fitting structure the finding names. Its Lemma 3.5 records that Fitting ideals commute with FLAT base change. IMPORTANTLY, on direct retrieval of the paper text I could NOT verify any statement that these ideals or loci commute with ARBITRARY base change; a search-engine summary asserted this, and I am recording that assertion as UNVERIFIED and not relying on it. The flat-versus-arbitrary distinction is exactly where 'over an arbitrary base' in the finding bites, so this failure to verify strengthens rather than weakens the finding. (3) Expected-codimension arithmetic (reviewer-computed, elementary): chi(N) = 1 - g = -5 forces complex ranks e and e+5, so the rank-drop locus has expected codimension g = 6, matching the codimension of the identity section in the relative Picard. The two structures therefore agree in expected codimension while remaining a priori distinct as schemes - necessary but not sufficient, which is the finding's precise content. DISCHARGE ROUTE AND ITS CURRENT STATUS. The natural discharge is: (a) base-change stability of the Brill-Noether/Fitting degeneracy structure, so that the relative locus is the pullback of a universal determinantal locus in Pic^0; plus (b) reducedness of that universal degree-zero locus, which for a single smooth curve follows from the Riemann-Kempf/Petri tangent-space formula T_L W^r_d = (Im mu_0)^perp, since for L = O_C the map mu_0 : H^0(O_C) tensor H^0(K) -> H^0(K) is an isomorphism and the tangent space is zero. PRIMARY VERIFICATION. (1) Semicontinuity: Stacks Project Lemma 36.32.1 (tag 0BDN) states that for f: X -> S proper of finite presentation and F of finite presentation and flat over S, the function s -> dim_{kappa(s)} H^i(X_s, F_s) commutes with arbitrary base change, is upper semi-continuous, and has locally constructible level sets; jumping loci are therefore genuine closed conditions, not artifacts removable by shrinking. (2) The only unconditional positive criterion in that section is Lemma 36.32.4 (tag 0D4E): if R^i f_* F = 0 for i > 0, then f_* F is locally free and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change - for a relative curve and a line bundle this is exactly the h^1 = 0 hypothesis. The two classical licenses are Grauert (h^i constant on a reduced base implies R^i locally free with base change; Hartshorne, Algebraic Geometry, GTM 52, III.12.9) and Grothendieck's cohomology-and-base-change theorem (Hartshorne III.12.11; Mumford, Abelian Varieties, II.5; EGA III 7.7.5). For g = 6, deg L = 4 = 2m + b the three admissible types give h^0 = 1 for (m,b) = (0,4); h^0 = 2 for (1,2), i.e. L = A + p + q with p,q the two base points and moving part the g^1_2; h^0 = 3 for (2,0), i.e. L = A^2 = 2 g^1_2. ATT-0096 clause (2)/CLM-0096-2 takes V to be a connected normal component of the distinct-support open U of the Abel–Jacobi incidence over the reduced balanced normalized Hurwitz stack H, then argues: étale monodromy through H_V⊂S_6 has [S_6:H_V] orbits of size |H_V|; a finite étale cover of a normal scheme is normal; irreducible components of a locally Noetherian normal scheme are open and closed; hence those orbits are the irreducible components, each of degree |H_V|. The cited facts are scheme-scoped. Stacks 58.7 (03SF) transfers the Galois-category language to finite étale morphisms of connected schemes. Stacks Lemma 58.11.2 (0BQL) says that a connected finite étale cover of a normal integral scheme is itself an integral normal scheme. Stacks Lemma 28.7.7 (033N) says a locally Noetherian scheme is normal if and only if it is a disjoint union of integral normal schemes. None of these tags applies to an algebraic stack. Normality of a stack is the smooth-atlas property: Stacks 100.7 (04YE) and Remark 100.7.3 (04YH) make 'normal' a smooth-local scheme property, so a stack is normal precisely when some (equivalently any) smooth atlas is a normal scheme. Étale morphisms of stacks are a separate, DM-restricted notion (Stacks 101.35/0CIK): they are not 'smooth of relative dimension 0', and the residual-gerbe examples [A^1/G_m] and [Spec k/μ_p] show that stacky finite/quasi-finite behaviour is not the scheme one. Residual gerbes exist under the Stacks 100.11 (06ML) hypotheses; their automorphism groups are the geometric inertia. Noohi (arXiv math/0201021v1, Thm 1.1) puts a homomorphism ω_x from Aut of the residue gerbe into π_1 of the stack, and identifies π_1(stack)/N with π_1 of the coarse space, N being generated by all such inertia images. Consequently inertia acts on the geometric fibre of a finite étale cover, in particular on the ordered S_6-fibre. If H_V is computed from coarse-space or atlas path monodromy without that groupoid/inertia action, the orbit count and the degrees need not match the irreducible components or representable degrees of the stack Z_V. Noohi moreover defines a covering space of a stack to be a finite étale representable morphism, so representability is an extra datum, not a formal consequence of writing 'S_6-torsor' in scheme language. The finding's rescue clauses are exactly the ones these sources license: (i) inertia-free, i.e. I_V→V an equivalence, so V is an algebraic space (Stacks Prop. 94.13.3/04SZ) and one reduces to FND-0132; or (ii) pull back to a normal scheme atlas, apply 03SF+0BQL+033N there, and descend along R=U×_V U while tracking how residual-gerbe automorphisms permute components. A third, equivalent, route is to take H_V as the image of the stacky π_1 so that inertia is already inside the monodromy; ATT-0096 does not do this. SCOPE SHARPENING. The finding is a proof-obligation obstruction, not a numerical counterexample: it does not assert that [S_6:H_V] fails when H_V is the stacky monodromy image and components/degrees are those of the stack. It asserts that the scheme-theoretic formula, as written and as used in CLM-0096-2, is not valid on a stack without one of the extra hypotheses. RELATION TO THE CORPUS. Complementary to corroborated FND-0132 (FAUD-0137 scoped the connected-to-irreducible upgrade to a connected locally Noetherian scheme; the missing piece here is stackiness/inertia, not normality). Complementary to FND-0127 (scheme-to-stack descent for Grauert/Abel–Jacobi identifications, not Galois component counts). Complementary to FND-0064 (existence of the stack-level S_6-torsor on pairwise-distinct sections) and FND-0075 (that torsor fails on coarse moduli when automorphisms permute marks; Q-coefficient cohomology descent is harmless, which does not salvage an integral/scheme-theoretic component-and-degree formula). Mandatory first reads of ATT-0101 and REV-0150 confirm the contested wording and also show that the attempt's formulas are already the correct ones. ATT-0101 theorem_statement and CLM-0101-3 write that Irr(Z_alpha) is indexed by 'the left cosets H_alpha\S_6'; argument section 3 says the monodromy orbits 'are precisely the left cosets H_alpha\G' and then, in the same paragraph, indexes a component by H_alpha g and computes its right-deck stabilizer as g^{-1}H_alpha g. CLM-0101-4's justification repeats 'right multiplication is transitive on left cosets and stabilizes H_alpha g through g^{-1}H_alpha g'. REV-0150 independently re-derives the orbits as the sets H_alpha g, confirms the stabilizer g^{-1}H_alpha g, and records FC-REV0150-COSET-SIDE as a nomenclature slip that 'does not affect the truth of the clause'; strongest_attack likewise says the notation H_alpha\S_6 together with the stabilizer computation pins the correct reading. Packet FND-0148 (corroborated) uses Irr(Z)=H\S_6 and 'indexed by left H_arith-cosets' with stabilizer only 'conjugate to H_arith', so it carries the same English mislabel but not a wrong conjugate. Independent public sources agree with the group-theoretic core under elementary nomenclature: Encyclopedia of Mathematics (oldid 35336) defines the left coset as aH={ah:h in H} and the right coset as Ha; Wikipedia Coset revision 1351557349 defines gH as a left coset, Hg as a right coset, writes G/H for {gH} and H\G for {Hg}, and states that the orbit of g under the left H-action (h,g)|->hg is the right coset Hg, while the orbit under the right H-action is the left coset gH. The same page records that left and right decompositions coincide if and only if H is normal, and that the product of left cosets is the quotient-group operation only in that case. The original candidate therefore overstates that right multiplication on S_6/H={gH} is 'not well defined at all': that product is well-defined precisely when H is normal in G, hence in particular for the normal subgroups {1}, A_6, and S_6 of S_6, and fails for every non-normal monodromy image. The conjugacy bookkeeping hazard is likewise sharpest when H is non-normal: the stabilizer of Hg under the right G-action is g^{-1}Hg, whereas gHg^{-1} is the stabilizer of gH under the left G-action, and these need not be the same conjugate. No contradiction with CONJ-0001, THM-0001 through THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001 (contradicts_claim_ids is empty). Compatible with the mathematical content of FND-0148 (H\S_6 indexing, degree |H|, stabilizer conjugate to H, arithmetic versus geometric monodromy) while correcting only the adjective 'left'. Compatible with FND-0132 (normality needed to pass from pi_0 to Irr) and with the confirmed ATT-0101 component clauses. Not a merge into FND-0148: that finding is the arithmetic/geometric monodromy distinction, not this typing discipline. Not retired as cosmetic: the English slip in ATT-0101 is harmless only because that artifact already writes Hg and g^{-1}Hg; downstream artifacts that take 'left cosets' literally as {gH} and then apply the right deck action, or that record the stabilizer as gHg^{-1} on the {Hg} indexing, are ill-typed. Mandatory first reads: ATT-0101 theorem_statement and Section 3 / CLM-0101-3 / CLM-0101-4, and REV-0150 checked_claims for those two clauses plus finding_candidate FC-REV0150-INDUCED-REP-ON-COMPONENTS (the exact source of FND-0152). ATT-0101 proves, and REV-0150 confirms, that Z_alpha -> U_alpha is a finite etale right S_6-torsor over a normal integral U_alpha, that Irr(Z_alpha) is the monodromy-orbit set of cardinality [S_6:H_alpha], that each component maps finite etale of degree |H_alpha| onto U_alpha, and that the right S_6-action is transitive on components with stabilizer conjugate to H_alpha. The induction formula is not stated in ATT-0101 (which explicitly records GAP-TATE and asserts no Hodge or Tate conclusion); it is a reviewer corollary. It is compatible with packet FND-0148 (H_alpha is arithmetic monodromy; here k is algebraically closed, so the arithmetic/geometric distinction is vacuous), FND-0151 (index set is the orbit set H_alpha\S_6 of left multiplication, i.e. right cosets H_alpha g, with stabilizer g^{-1}H_alpha g), FND-0132 (normality is load-bearing for Irr=pi_0), FND-0144 (the formula is scheme-level and does not extend to stacks with inertia), FND-0053 (induction does not force Tate local systems), and FND-0075 (Q-coefficients, no integral or coarse-space descent). Independent primary checks. (1) Finite-group induction: the Q[S_6]-module attached to a transitive permutation of summands with stabilizer H_alpha and H_alpha-module V on the identity-coset summand is Ind_{H_alpha}^{S_6} V = Q[S_6] tensor_{Q[H_alpha]} V (Wikipedia, Induced representation, algebraic construction; Serre GTM 42). Right multiplication by g is a U_alpha-automorphism of the torsor, so all components are isomorphic as U_alpha-schemes and F(Z_alpha) is that induced object for any additive S_6-equivariant F. (2) Residual Galois: Z_alpha^1 is connected of degree |H_alpha| over U_alpha with Aut_{U_alpha}(Z_alpha^1) equal to the component stabilizer H_alpha, hence Z_alpha^1 -> U_alpha is a Galois cover with group H_alpha (Stacks Project Tag 03SF, equivalent conditions (1)-(4)). (3) Invariants: for an n-sheeted covering given by a group action, Hatcher Algebraic Topology Proposition 3G.1 states that with coefficients in a field of characteristic 0 or prime to n, pullback is injective onto the deck-invariants; equivalently, MathOverflow 57076 (Sprehn) records that if |G| is a unit in the coefficient ring then H^*(X/G) -> H^*(X)^G is an isomorphism (Milnor Characteristic Classes exercise). Thus H^*(U_alpha;Q) = H^*(Z_alpha^1;Q)^{H_alpha}, and Frobenius reciprocity gives the S_6-invariant consistency check. The same transfer applies to ordinary homology; Borel-Moore homology is included only as an additive S_6-equivariant functor (finite-sheeted lifts preserve locally finite chains), not as a separate Hatcher citation. Algebraic deck maps are morphisms of mixed Hodge structures, so the Q-linear identifications are MHS identifications. Wording corrections required before promotion: the original '=' must be an isomorphism of S_6-objects; components must be indexed by H_alpha\S_6 as in FND-0151, not by a mislabelled left-coset set; and consequence (i) overstates when it says uncomputed H_alpha is the only obstruction — H_alpha determines the induction functor and the component count, but the H_alpha-object F(Z_alpha^1) remains an independent geometric/Hodge input (GAP-TATE). Consequence (ii) is correct and is retained. Distinct from FND-0148, FND-0151, FND-0053, and FND-0075: do not merge. Promote from candidate to corroborated; evidence_class upgraded from adversarial_review to primary_source.

The contested passage is ATT-0113 Lemma 4.1 / theorem clause (D) / CLM-0113-5, which infers Gr^W_16 of each compact-support Leray term E_2^{p,q}=H_c^p(X^bal; R^q f_! Q) (p+q=16, p<=14) from Lemma 3.1 / CLM-0113-4, i.e. from Gr^W_p H_c^p(X^bal;Q)=0. REV-0160's strongest attack is correct on that passage: the general weight ceiling supplies only weights <= p+q=16 and therefore permits Gr^W_16. Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II, Corollaire 3.2.15(ii) (Publ. Math. IHES 40 (1971); doi 10.1007/BF02684692) places ordinary H^n of a smooth variety in weights >= n (Hodge numbers nonzero only for p<=n, q<=n, and p+q>=n); Poincare duality then gives the constant-coefficient compact-support ceiling weights(H_c^p)<=p used in Lemma 3.1. Saito's six-functor weight calculus, recorded as Properties 2.1.E--G in Peters--Saito arXiv:0812.2132v1 (published Nagoya Math. J. 206 (2012), doi 10.1215/00277630-1548466) and in Schnell arXiv:1405.3096v1, states that f_! does not increase weights, so if V has weights <=w then H_c^p(B;V) has weights <=p+w and Gr^W_{p+w} is allowed. Peters--Saito's main theorem identifies the lowest weight of H^k(U,V) for a polarizable VHS of weight n with the image of intersection cohomology of the intermediate extension, which is pure of weight k+n and is not a functor of H^k(U;Q); dually, Gr^W_{p+w} H_c^p(B;V) is that intersection/top-weight piece. A weight-w summand supported on a p-dimensional stratum likewise contributes in weight p+w. The parenthetical alternative in ATT-0113 Lemma 4.1 (localization of a bounded complex against Y=X\X^bal) is not supplied: R^q f_! Q lives on X^bal and is not extended across Y. Dual Artin vanishing H_c^i(X,F)=0 for i<dim X on the affine 15-fold holds for locally constant F on X, not for general constructible F (skyscrapers) and not for j_! of a local system from a proper open. Exception, which the original candidate omitted: if R^q f_! Q is a constant Tate twist then Kunneth does transfer the vanishing, and this likely applies to the q=4 term (connected affine-surface fibres give R^4 f_! Q isomorphic to Q(-2)), but not to the typically nonconstant q=2,3 terms built from H^1/H^2 of the varying discriminant. CLM-0113-4 stands for constant Q. No contradiction with CONJ-0001, THM-0001--THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. The exact contested passage in ATT-0114, Lemma 1.1/CLM-0114-1, derives the injection from the compact-support localization sequence, the bound wt H_c^{m-1}(Y) <= m-1, and strictness of the weight filtration; it then dualizes using H_m^{BM}=H_c^m dual with no Tate twist. That reasoning is correct for separated finite-type C-schemes. REV-0161's strongest attack concerned a possible hidden identification of discriminant-complement cohomology with projective-bundle cohomology. The attack does not contradict the lemma: localization proves only that the kernel of H_c^m(V) -> H_c^m(X) has weights at most m-1, hence gives an injection after Gr_m^W; it gives neither an isomorphism of the full groups nor a Leray statement with nonconstant coefficients. The audit does, however, reject the originating attempt's unqualified Deligne-Mumford-stack scope. Deligne's simplicial construction supports ordinary stack cohomology but is not, by itself, a cited construction of compactly supported cohomology or Borel-Moore homology for stacks. Tubach's later six-functor theory supplies a possible modern stack-level repair, but that is additional infrastructure not established in ATT-0114. No independently retrieved primary source explicitly verified the proposed rational compact-support comparison with coarse spaces in the exact Betti mixed-Hodge conventions used there. The promoted statement is therefore narrowed to schemes; this still covers the load-bearing applications U subset A and Z^(1) subset D identified in ATT-0114 and REV-0161. Reduced structure on Y is harmless for rational Betti cohomology. With H_m^{BM}(Z;Q) defined as H_c^m(Z;Q)^vee, no Tate twist occurs; because H_c^m has weights at most m, its dual has weights at least -m, so W_{-m}H_m^{BM} is the dual of Gr_m^W H_c^m. This also fixes the direction: dualizing the corner injection gives T_m(X) -> T_m(V) surjective. The finding is distinct from FND-0164 because it uses a degree drop from m to m-1 on the fixed closed complement, not a transfer of a constant-coefficient weight bound to a nonconstant Leray coefficient object.

Three wording corrections applied to the candidate. (i) 'the Poincare dual of the RED-0001 open input' is loose: K is the Q-linear Hodge-structure DUAL of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) under Borel-Moore/compact-support duality; Poincare duality is the separate twisted identification W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16} = W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) of FND-0001. The adjudicated statement separates the two maps. (ii) The candidate attributes the tautology to semisimplicity. Semisimplicity is not needed: for a pure weight-16 Q-Hodge structure V, 'V is a direct sum of Q(-8)' and 'V is spanned by its Hodge (8,8)-classes' are the same condition V_C = V^{8,8} by definition of Hodge type. Semisimplicity (packet FND-0033) is what rules out extension gaps at this corner; it is not what makes the (8,8)-spanning restatement contentless. (iii) 'is not equivalent to' overreaches as a mathematical assertion. Non-equivalence of two statements cannot be established here, because if the RED-0001 target is Tate both sides are true and the biconditional holds vacuously. The defensible content is that the biconditional is unproved and is a non-sequitur in the load-bearing direction, and that the missing input is a support-exhaustion statement. One substantive correction to REV-0163, carried into the adjudicated statement. The review's 'neither necessary nor sufficient' is only half right, and which half depends on a reading the attempt never fixes. Fix a closed support Y in M_{6,6} carrying Z. Gr^W is exact on mixed Hodge structures, so the Borel-Moore localization sequence H^{BM}_{16}(Y) -> H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}) -> H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6} minus Y) stays exact after applying Gr^W_{-16} = W_{-16} at the lowest weight. Under reading (i), 'the contribution supported on Z' = the image of the first map, a SUB-object of the RED-0001 group: then K Tate implies that contribution Tate (sub-objects of a type-(8,8) structure are type (8,8)), so Z-Tate is necessary, and only sufficiency fails, requiring Tate-ness or vanishing of the piece injecting into the complement's group. Under reading (ii), 'the contribution' = Gr^W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y) itself, an upstairs group of which only the image is constrained: then neither direction follows. So the review is right that the reduction collapses, but its blanket 'neither necessary nor sufficient' holds only under reading (ii); the ambiguity between the two readings is itself part of the defect and is now recorded.

Public-source cross-check. The weight-graded compact-support machinery invoked above (Deligne weight spectral sequence for H^*_c(M_{g,n};Q), E_2-degeneration, and the duality gr_k H^*_c(M_{g,n}) = gr_{6g-8+2n}H^{6g-6+2n-*}(M_{g,n})^vee displayed as equation (9) in section 2.7) is standard and publicly documented in arXiv:2110.05711v2, which supports the corner bookkeeping but contains no support-exhaustion or algebraicity theorem for the (6,6) degree-16 corner. arXiv:1805.10186 (Chan-Galatius-Payne, JAMS 34 (2021) 565-594) fixes the opposite, top-weight corner and so cannot supply the missing input, consistent with FND-0032. Payne's survey arXiv:2605.20453 frames Hodge/Tate-conjecture statements for moduli of curves as verified in a range of cases via the boundary stratification with open problems remaining, i.e. no general algebraicity theorem is available to license the Hodge-to-algebraic upgrade. The Hodge conjecture itself is proved only in the (1,1) case and low-dimensional or special situations and is open for higher codimension in general, so the codimension-8 upgrade on the 21-dimensional Mbar_{6,6} is an assumption, not an equivalence.

Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II, Lemma 4.2.3, states semisimplicity and proves that a polarized homogeneous Hodge structure splits off any subobject by its orthogonal complement; specialized to a point, every epimorphism of polarizable pure Q-Hodge structures splits. The source record's SHA-256 is over the 20,222 UTF-8 bytes of the live fetched textual extraction of the public PDF, not a purported digest of the server's raw PDF binary. Cross-checking FND-0180, FND-0185, and FND-0033 supplies the geometric quotient, purity, and polarizability hypotheses. The result is a categorical sharpening and exact reformulation of FND-0185, not a separate obstruction or new geometric input, so it should be merged into FND-0185 rather than promoted independently.

S_j is open in Y^(j), so Y^(j+1) := (Y^(j) minus S_j)_red is closed in Y^(j) hence in X, and S_j = Y^(j) cap (X minus Y^(j+1)) is closed in X minus Y^(j+1). Y^(j+1) is the union of the lower-dimensional components with the proper closed subsets C_a minus S_j, so dim Y^(j+1) <= d_j - 1; strict decrease of a nonnegative integer forces termination. The final published Canning-Larson-Payne article resolves the latter two directly: Lemma 3.1(a) states the quotient is the direct sum of W_k H^{k-n}(M_g;mathbb V_lambda) tensor V_{lambda^T}, and its proof uses the closed universal curve, smooth-proper Leray degeneration, the all-R^1 Kunneth term, Petersen-Tavakol-Yin projectors, and symplectic contractions. Thus (g,n,k)=(6,6,26) gives ordinary degree 20 and weight index 26; it does not involve the mixed R^1 of the punctured forgetful map discussed in FND-0037. Church-Farb-Putman explicitly record Harer's result vcd(Mod_g)=4g-5 and the consequent vanishing H^i(Mod_g;V tensor Q)=0 for i>4g-5 and arbitrary Mod_g-modules V. Formally, choose a torsion-free normal finite-index subgroup Gamma of Mod_6 with cd(Gamma)=19. Then H^20(Gamma;mathbb V_lambda)=0, and Hochschild-Serre for the finite quotient Mod_6/Gamma collapses over Q because finite-group invariants are exact, giving H^20(Mod_6;mathbb V_lambda)=0. Hence W_26 of that zero group is zero. This is compatible with FND-0035: FND-0035 only blocks an above-vcd argument at the target degree 26 on Mod_{6,6}, whereas the present application is degree 20>19 on Mod_6. It also does not contradict RED-0001, THM-0005, or any claim listed in contradicts_claim_ids. No equivalent adjudicated finding was found, so merging is unwarranted.
